title.zh: 卷79 列傳第44 外戚
title.raw: 卷79 列傳第44 外戚 Volume 79 Biographies 44: Imperial Affines

sentences.zh: 隋書卷七十九列傳第四十四

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 79, Biographies 44
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 79, Biographies 44

sentences.zh: ○外戚

translations.literal: ○ Imperial Affines
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Affines

sentences.zh: 曆觀前代外戚之家，乘母后之權以取高位厚秩者多矣，然而鮮有克終之美，必罹顛覆之患，何哉？

translations.literal: Looking through past ages at households of imperial affines, those who rode the empress dowager's power to obtain high rank and rich stipends have been many, yet few have had the beauty of completing their course, and all must suffer the calamity of overthrow—why?
translations.idiomatic: A survey of past dynasties shows that many families of imperial affines used the empress dowager's authority to win high office and lavish stipends, yet few enjoyed a happy end and nearly all met ruin—why is this?

sentences.zh: 皆由乎無德而尊，不知紀極，忽于滿盈之戒，罔念高危之咎，故鬼瞰其室，憂必及之。

translations.literal: All stem from being honored without virtue, not knowing limits, neglecting the warning against fullness, and forgetting the blame of standing in perilous height; therefore ghosts peer into their houses, and sorrow must reach them.
translations.idiomatic: It is because they were exalted without virtue, knew no bounds, ignored the warning against excess, and forgot the peril of standing too high—so that, as the saying goes, when ghosts gaze upon a house, grief is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 夫其誠著艱難，功宣社稷，不以謙沖自牧，未免顛蹶之禍，而況道不足以濟時，仁不足以利物，自矜於己，以富貴驕人者乎？

translations.literal: As for those whose sincerity showed in hardship and whose achievements proclaimed the altars of state, if they did not restrain themselves with humility, they still could not escape the disaster of a fall—how much more those whose Way was insufficient to rescue the age, whose benevolence was insufficient to benefit things, who prided themselves and used wealth and rank to look down on others?
translations.idiomatic: Even men whose loyalty was proved in adversity and whose service to the state was real, if they did not govern themselves with humility, could not escape disaster—how much less those whose conduct could not save the times, whose kindness could not benefit others, yet who prided themselves on wealth and rank?

sentences.zh: 此呂、霍、上官、閻、梁、竇、鄧所以繼踵而亡滅者也。

translations.literal: This is why the clans of Lü, Huo, Shangguan, Yan, Liang, Dou, and Deng followed one another in succession to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the houses of Lü, Huo, Shangguan, Yan, Liang, Dou, and Deng fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 昔文皇潛躍之際，獻後便相推轂，煬帝大橫方兆，蕭妃密勿經綸，是以恩禮綢繆，始終不易。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Emperor Wen was rising in concealment, Empress Xian at once helped push the carriage; when Emperor Yang's great mandate was just appearing, Consort Xiao worked closely on state affairs—therefore favor and ritual were thickly woven and never changed from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was still making his rise, Empress Xian already helped drive his cause forward; when Emperor Yang's great mandate was only beginning to show, Consort Xiao took a close hand in affairs of state. For this reason imperial favor and ceremony remained constant from first to last.

sentences.zh: 然內外親戚，莫預朝權，昆弟在位，亦無殊寵。

translations.literal: Yet among kin within and without, none took part in court power; brothers who held office likewise received no special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet neither the maternal nor the paternal kin shared in court power, and brothers who held office received no extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 至於居擅玉堂，家稱金穴，暉光戚裡，重灼四方，將三司以比儀，命五侯而同拜者，終始一代，寂無聞焉。

translations.literal: As for those who monopolized the jade hall, whose households were called gold caves, whose brilliance lit the imperial affines' quarter and whose weight scorched the four quarters, who treated the Three Excellencies as peers and ordered the Five Marquises to bow together—through the whole dynasty there was not a whisper of such things.
translations.idiomatic: As for the abuses of old—monopolizing the halls of state, households famed as treasure vaults, kin whose splendor dazzled the realm, treating the Three Excellencies as equals and commanding the Five Marquises to bow as one—through the entire Sui dynasty one hears nothing of the kind.

sentences.zh: 考之前王，可謂矯其弊矣。

translations.literal: Comparing with former kings, one may say they corrected this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with earlier rulers, the Sui emperors may be said to have corrected this abuse.

sentences.zh: 故雖時經擾攘，無有陷於不義，市朝遷貿，而皆得以保全。

translations.literal: Therefore, although the times passed through turmoil, none fell into injustice; though markets and courts shifted and changed, all were able to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Thus even when the realm was in turmoil, none of the affinal kin were drawn into disloyalty; though power changed hands in court and market, they all survived.

sentences.zh: 比夫憑藉寵私，階緣恩澤，乘其非據，旋就顛隕者，豈可同日而言哉！

translations.literal: Compared with those who relied on private favor, climbed by grace and bounty, seized what was not theirs, and at once met overturn and ruin—how can they be spoken of on the same day!
translations.idiomatic: How can they be mentioned in the same breath as those who leaned on private favor, climbed by imperial grace, seized what was not theirs, and were soon overthrown!

sentences.zh: 此所謂愛之以禮，能改覆車。

translations.literal: This is what is called loving them by ritual and being able to change the overturned cart.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by loving kin with proper restraint and learning from the wreck of the overturned cart.

sentences.zh: 輒敘其事，為《外戚傳》雲。

translations.literal: I therefore narrate these affairs and make the 《Biographies of Imperial Affines》.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore set out these affairs in the 《Biographies of Imperial Affines》.

sentences.zh: ○高祖外家呂氏

translations.literal: ○ The Lü Clan, Gaozu's Maternal Kin
translations.idiomatic: The Lü Clan, Gaozu's Maternal Kin

sentences.zh: 高祖外家呂氏，其族蓋微，平齊之後，求訪不知所在。

translations.literal: Gaozu's maternal kin, the Lü clan—their lineage was quite humble; after the pacification of Qi, searches were made but their whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's mother's family, the Lü clan, was of humble standing; after the conquest of Qi, inquiries failed to locate them.

sentences.zh: 至開皇初，濟南郡上言，有男子呂永吉，自稱有姑字苦桃，為楊忠妻。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Kaihuang, Jinan commandery reported that a man named Lü Yongji claimed he had an aunt styled Kutao who was the wife of Yang Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Jinan commandery reported that a man named Lü Yongji claimed an aunt, styled Kutao, who had been the wife of Yang Zhong.

sentences.zh: 勘驗知是舅子，始追贈外祖雙周為上柱國、太尉、八州諸軍事、青州刺史，封齊郡公，諡曰敬，外祖母姚氏為齊敬公夫人。

translations.literal: On investigation he was known to be a nephew by the maternal line; only then were posthumous honors granted to the maternal grandfather Shuang Zhou as Supreme Pillar of State, Grand Commandant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in eight provinces, and Governor of Qing Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi commandery with posthumous title Jing; the maternal grandmother, Lady Yao, was made Lady of Duke Jing of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation confirmed him as a maternal nephew. Gaozu then posthumously honored his maternal grandfather Shuang Zhou as Supreme Pillar of State, Grand Commandant, commander of military affairs in eight provinces, and Governor of Qingzhou, enfeoffing him as Duke of Qi with the posthumous title Jing; his maternal grandmother, the Yao clan, was titled Lady of Duke Jing of Qi.

sentences.zh: 詔並改葬，于齊州立廟，置守塚十家。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them both reburied, a temple established in Qi province, and ten households appointed to guard the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered their remains reinterred, a temple built in Qi province, and ten households assigned to tend the graves.

sentences.zh: 以永吉襲爵，留在京師。

translations.literal: Yongji was made to inherit the title and remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji inherited the title and remained at court.

sentences.zh: 大業中，授上党郡太守，性識庸劣，職務不理。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was appointed Governor of Shangdang commandery; his nature and understanding were coarse and inferior, and he did not attend to his duties.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye he was appointed governor of Shangdang commandery, but his mind was dull and he neglected his office.

sentences.zh: 後去官，不知所終。

translations.literal: Later he left office, and no one knows how he ended.
translations.idiomatic: He later left office, and nothing more is known of him.

sentences.zh: 永吉從父道貴，性尤頑騃，言詞鄙陋。

translations.literal: Yongji's paternal uncle Daogui was especially stubborn and dull, and his speech was vulgar and crude.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji's uncle Daogui was even more obstinate and slow-witted, and his speech was coarse.

sentences.zh: 初自鄉里征入長安，上見之悲泣。

translations.literal: When he was first summoned from the countryside into Chang'an, the Emperor saw him and wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first summoned from the countryside to Chang'an, the emperor wept at the sight of him.

sentences.zh: 道貴略無戚容，但連呼高祖名，雲：「種末定不可偷，大似苦桃姊。

translations.literal: Daogui showed hardly any look of kinship feeling, but only kept calling Gaozu by his personal name, saying: "The seed is not yet fixed and cannot be stolen—it greatly resembles Elder Sister Kutao."
translations.idiomatic: Daogui showed little sign of emotion, but kept calling the emperor by his personal name and said, "The breed isn't settled yet—you can't steal that. You're just like Elder Sister Kutao."

sentences.zh: 」是後數犯忌諱，動致違忤，上甚耽之。

translations.literal: After this he repeatedly violated taboos and constantly caused offense; the Emperor was greatly troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he repeatedly violated taboo and gave offense at every turn, until the emperor could bear him no longer.

sentences.zh: 乃命高熲厚加供給，不許接對朝士。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered Gao Jiong to supply him generously and forbade him to meet or converse with court officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Gao Jiong to provide for him generously but forbade him to associate with officials at court.

sentences.zh: 拜上儀同三司，出為濟南太守，令即之任，斷其入朝。

translations.literal: He was appointed Senior Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, sent out as Governor of Jinan, ordered to take up his post at once, and cut off from coming to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Senior Palace Attendant of the Third Rank and sent out as governor of Jinan with orders to take up his post immediately and never return to court.

sentences.zh: 道貴還至本郡，高自崇重，每與人言，自稱皇舅。

translations.literal: When Daogui returned to his home commandery, he held himself in high esteem; whenever he spoke with others he called himself the emperor's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Back in his home commandery, Daogui held himself in high regard and told everyone he met that he was the emperor's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 數將儀衛出入閭裡，從故人游宴，官民鹹苦之。

translations.literal: He often led guards and attendants in and out of the lanes, followed old acquaintances in feasting and revelry, and officials and commoners alike suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: He often paraded with guards through the streets, caroused with old friends, and officials and commoners alike found him unbearable.

sentences.zh: 後郡廢，終於家，子孫無聞焉。

translations.literal: Later the commandery was abolished; he died at home, and nothing is heard of his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery was later abolished, he died at home, and nothing is known of his descendants.

sentences.zh: 獨孤羅弟陀

translations.literal: Dugu Luo; his younger brother Tuo
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Luo and His Younger Brother Tuo

sentences.zh: 獨孤羅，字羅仁，雲中人也。

translations.literal: Dugu Luo, styled Luoren, was a man of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Luo, styled Luoren, was a native of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 父信，初仕魏為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xin at first served Wei as Governor of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin had first served Northern Wei as governor of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 武帝之入關也，信棄父母妻子西歸長安，曆職顯貴，羅由是遂為高氏所囚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Xin abandoned parents, wife, and children and returned west to Chang'an, passing through offices to eminent rank; Luo for this reason was then imprisoned by the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou entered the passes, Xin left his parents, wife, and children behind and went west to Chang'an, rising to high office; Luo was therefore left behind and imprisoned by the Gao clan of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 信後仕周為大司馬。

translations.literal: Xin later served Zhou as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Xin later served the Zhou court as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 及信為宇文護所誅，羅始見釋，寓居中山，孤貧無以自給。

translations.literal: When Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was only then released; he lodged in Zhongshan, alone and poor, with no means to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was at last released. He lived in Zhongshan, alone and destitute, with no means of support.

sentences.zh: 齊將獨孤永業以宗族之故，見而哀之，為買田宅，遺以資畜。

translations.literal: The Qi general Dugu Yongye, because of clan ties, saw him and pitied him, bought fields and a house for him, and gave him livestock and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi general Dugu Yongye, a kinsman, took pity on him, bought him land and a house, and gave him livestock and supplies.

sentences.zh: 初，信入關之後，複娶二妻，郭氏生子六人，善、穆、藏、順、陀、整，崔氏生獻皇后。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Xin entered the passes he took two wives again: the Guo clan bore six sons—Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng; the Cui clan bore Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin entered the passes he had taken two more wives: Lady Guo bore six sons—Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng—and Lady Cui bore the future Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 及齊亡，高祖為定州總管，獻皇后遣人尋羅，得之，相見悲不自勝，侍御者皆泣。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, Gaozu was Regional Inspector of Dingzhou; Empress Xian sent men to seek Luo, found him, and on meeting grieved beyond control—those attending all wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell, Gaozu was regional inspector of Dingzhou. Empress Xian sent men to find Luo; when they met, her grief was overwhelming and all who attended wept.

sentences.zh: 於是厚遺車馬財物。

translations.literal: Thereupon she sent him generously carriages, horses, and goods.
translations.idiomatic: She then sent him generous gifts of carriages, horses, and goods.

sentences.zh: 未幾，周武帝以羅功臣子，久淪異域，征拜楚安郡太守。

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Wu of Zhou, because Luo was the son of a meritorious minister long lost in a foreign land, summoned and appointed him Governor of Chu'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Wu of Zhou, noting that Luo was the son of a meritorious minister long stranded in enemy territory, summoned him and appointed him governor of Chu'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 以疾去官，歸於京師。

translations.literal: Because of illness he left office and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to resign and return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 諸弟見羅少長貧賤，每輕侮之，不以兄禮事也。

translations.literal: His younger brothers, seeing that Luo from youth had been poor and lowly, always treated him lightly and did not serve him with the rites due an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers, knowing he had grown up poor and obscure, often slighted him and did not treat him with the respect owed an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 然性長者，亦不與諸弟校競長短，後由是重之。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was a man of forbearance and did not compete with his brothers over who was greater or lesser; later for this reason they came to respect him.
translations.idiomatic: But he was by nature forbearing and did not contend with his brothers; for this they later came to respect him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，拜儀同，常置左右。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Luo was appointed Palace Attendant and regularly kept at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor, Luo was appointed Palace Attendant and kept constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 既受禪，下詔追贈羅父信官爵曰：「褒德累行，往代通規，追遠慎終，前王盛典。

translations.literal: After receiving the abdication, an edict was issued to posthumously grant Luo's father Xin offices and titles, saying: "Commending virtue and heaping up conduct is the common rule of past ages; pursuing the distant and being careful at the end is the great ceremony of former kings."
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, he issued an edict posthumously honoring Luo's father Xin, which read: "To praise accumulated virtue is the constant practice of former ages; to honor the dead and complete the rites is the great ceremony of ancient kings."

sentences.zh: 故柱國信，風宇高曠，獨秀生民，睿哲居宗，清猷映世。

translations.literal: "The former Pillar of State Xin had bearing lofty and broad, standing alone among the living; sagely wisdom held the clan's center, and pure plans shone upon the age."
translations.idiomatic: "The former Pillar of State Xin bore himself with lofty grace, stood apart among men, held sagely wisdom at the clan's center, and whose pure designs illuminated his age."

sentences.zh: 宏謀長策，道著於弼諧，緯義經仁，事深於拯濟。

translations.literal: "Grand designs and far-reaching policies—his Way was manifest in assisting harmony; weaving righteousness and threading benevolence, his service went deep in rescuing and aiding."
translations.idiomatic: "His grand designs and far-reaching policies made his Way manifest in aiding the throne; in weaving righteousness and threading benevolence, his service went deep in rescuing the realm."

sentences.zh: 方當宣風廊廟，亮采臺階，而運屬艱危，功高弗賞，眷言令範，事切於心。

translations.literal: "Just as he was about to spread influence in the hall and court and display his brilliance on the steps, fate met with hardship and peril; his merit was high yet went unrewarded—recalling his fine example touches the heart."
translations.idiomatic: "Just as he was to spread his influence in the halls of state and display his brilliance on the steps of power, fate turned harsh; his merit went unrewarded—yet memory of his fine example still moves the heart."

sentences.zh: 今景運初開，椒闈肅建，載懷塗山之義，無忘褒、紀之典。

translations.literal: "Now as the bright fortune first opens and the pepper chambers are solemnly established, bearing in mind the meaning of Mount Tu and not forgetting the ceremonies of Bao and Ji."
translations.idiomatic: "Now, as a new reign begins and the inner palace is duly established, mindful of the example of Mount Tu and unforgetting the rites owed to worthy forebears."

sentences.zh: 可贈太師、上柱國、冀定等十州刺史、趙國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: "—he may be granted Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of State, Governor of ten provinces including Ji and Ding, Duke of Zhao, with a fief of ten thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: "—let him be posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of State, governor of ten provinces including Ji and Ding, and Duke of Zhao, with a fief of ten thousand households."

sentences.zh: 」其諸弟以羅母沒齊，先無夫人之號，不當承襲。

translations.literal: " His younger brothers, because Luo's mother had died in Qi and had never held the title of Lady, ought not to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: " His younger brothers argued that because Luo's mother had died in Qi without ever receiving the title of Lady, he ought not inherit the dukedom.

sentences.zh: 上以問後，後曰：「羅誠嫡長，不可誣也。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the empress; the empress said: "Luo is truly the eldest legitimate son—it cannot be denied."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the empress, who replied, "Luo is truly the eldest legitimate son—that cannot be denied."

sentences.zh: 」於是襲爵趙國公。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he inherited the title Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: " Luo therefore inherited the title Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以其弟善為河內郡公，穆為金泉縣公，藏為武平縣公，陀為武喜縣公，整為千牛備身。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shan was made Duke of Henei commandery, Mu Duke of Jinquan county, Zang Duke of Wuping county, Tuo Duke of Wuxi county, and Zheng a guard of the Thousand-Ox.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shan was made Duke of Henei, Mu Duke of Jinquan county, Zang Duke of Wuping county, Tuo Duke of Wuxi county, and Zheng a guard of the Thousand-Ox.

sentences.zh: 擢拜羅為左領左右將軍，尋遷左衛將軍，前後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: Luo was promoted and appointed General of the Left Retinue of the Left and Right, soon transferred to General of the Left Guard; rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was promoted to General of the Left Retinue, soon transferred to General of the Left Guard, and showered with rewards beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 久而出為涼州總管，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: After a long time he went out as Regional Inspector of Liangzhou and advanced to Supreme Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out as regional inspector of Liangzhou and advanced to Supreme Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，征拜左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Renshou he was recalled and appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，改封蜀國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Luo's title was changed to Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office and was given the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子纂嗣，仕至河陽郡尉。

translations.literal: His son Zuan inherited; he served up to Commandant of Heyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuan inherited the title and rose to commandant of Heyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 纂弟武都，大業末，亦為河陽郡尉。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Wudu, at the end of Daye, also became Commandant of Heyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother Wudu likewise became commandant of Heyang commandery at the end of Daye.

sentences.zh: 庶長子開遠，宇文化及之弑逆也，裴虔通率賊入成象殿，宿衛兵士皆從逆，開遠時為千牛，與獨孤盛力戰於閤下，為賊所執，賊義而舍之。

translations.literal: The eldest son by a concubine, Kaiyuan—at Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Pei Qiantong led rebels into the Chengxian Hall; the palace guards all followed the rebellion. Kaiyuan was then a guard of the Thousand-Ox; he and Dugu Sheng fought fiercely below the gate-tower, were seized by the rebels, and the rebels in righteousness released them.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son by a concubine, Kaiyuan, was serving as a guard of the Thousand-Ox when Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor. Pei Qiantong led the rebels into the Chengxian Hall, and the palace guards joined the revolt. Kaiyuan and Dugu Sheng fought fiercely below the gate-tower, were captured, but the rebels, respecting their courage, let them go.

sentences.zh: 善後官至柱國。

translations.literal: Shan later reached the office of Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Shan later rose to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 卒，子覽嗣，仕至左候衛將軍，大業末卒。

translations.literal: He died; his son Lan inherited and served up to General of the Left Garrison Guard; he died at the end of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his son Lan inherited and rose to General of the Left Garrison Guard; he died at the end of Daye.

sentences.zh: 獨孤陀，字黎邪。

translations.literal: Dugu Tuo, styled Lixie.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Tuo, styled Lixie.

sentences.zh: 仕周胥附上士，坐父徙蜀郡十餘年。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as a Senior Attendant of the Palace Retinue; because of his father he was banished to Shu commandery for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Zhou court as a senior attendant of the palace retinue and, because of his father's case, was banished to Shu commandery for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 宇文護被誅，始歸長安。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Hu was executed, he at last returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Hu was executed, he was at last allowed to return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜上開府、右領左右將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Tuo was appointed Senior Opening Grandee and General of the Right Retinue of the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Tuo was appointed Senior Opening Grandee and General of the Right Retinue.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為郢州刺史，進位上大將軍，累轉延州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time he went out as Inspector of Ying province, advanced to Grand General, and was transferred in succession to Inspector of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out as inspector of Ying province, advanced to Grand General, and later transferred to inspector of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 好左道。

translations.literal: He was fond of heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to heterodox cult practices.

sentences.zh: 其妻母先事貓鬼，因轉入其家。

translations.literal: His wife's mother had first served the cat-demon, and the practice thereby passed into his household.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's mother had first practiced the cat-demon cult, and the rite passed into his household.

sentences.zh: 上微聞而不之信也。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard a little of it but did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard rumors but did not believe them.

sentences.zh: 會獻皇后及楊素妻鄭氏俱有疾，召醫者視之，皆曰：「此貓鬼疾也。

translations.literal: It happened that Empress Xian and Yang Su's wife, the Zheng clan, both fell ill; physicians were summoned to examine them, and all said: "This is cat-demon sickness."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xian and Yang Su's wife Lady Zheng both fell ill, physicians were summoned and all declared, "This is cat-demon sickness."

sentences.zh: 」上以陀後之異母弟，陀妻楊素之異母妹，由是意陀所為，陰令其兄穆以情喻之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, because Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and Tuo's wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, therefore suspected Tuo's doing and secretly ordered his elder brother Mu to explain the matter to him by feeling.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, noting that Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and that Tuo's wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, suspected Tuo and secretly had his brother Mu reason with him.

sentences.zh: 上又避左右諷陀，陀言無有。

translations.literal: The Emperor also, apart from attendants, admonished Tuo indirectly; Tuo said there was nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also spoke to him privately, hinting at the charge, but Tuo denied everything.

sentences.zh: 上不悅，左轉遷州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased and transferred him to the left as Inspector of Qian province.
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor demoted him to inspector of Qian province.

sentences.zh: 出怨言。

translations.literal: He uttered resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: He began to voice complaints.

sentences.zh: 上令左僕射高熲、納言蘇威、大理正皇甫孝緒、大理丞楊遠等雜治之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, Supporter of Speech Su Wei, Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Huangfu Xiaoxu, Vice Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Yang Yuan, and others jointly to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, Supporter of Speech Su Wei, Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Huangfu Xiaoxu, Vice Chief Yang Yuan, and others to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 陀婢徐阿尼言，本從陀母家來，常事貓鬼。

translations.literal: Tuo's maid Xu Ani said she had originally come from Tuo's mother's household and had constantly served the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's maid Xu Ani testified that she had come from his mother's household and had long served the cat-demon cult.

sentences.zh: 每以子日夜祀之。

translations.literal: Every night at the hour of zi she sacrificed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Every night at the hour of zi she performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 言子者鼠也。

translations.literal: "Zi" means rat.
translations.idiomatic: The word zi here refers to the rat.

sentences.zh: 其貓鬼每殺人者，所死家財物潛移於畜貓鬼家。

translations.literal: Whenever the cat-demon killed someone, the goods and property of the dead household were secretly transferred to the household that kept the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the cat-demon killed someone, the victim's wealth was secretly transferred to the household that kept the demon.

sentences.zh: 陀嘗從家中素酒，其妻曰：「無錢可酤。

translations.literal: Tuo once asked for plain wine from the household; his wife said: "There is no money to buy any."
translations.idiomatic: Tuo once asked for wine at home; his wife replied, "We have no money to buy any."

sentences.zh: 」陀因謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向越公家，使我足錢也。

translations.literal: " Tuo thereupon said to Ani: "You can make the cat-demon go to the Duke of Yue's household so that I have enough money."
translations.idiomatic: " Tuo then told Ani, "Send the cat-demon to the Duke of Yue's house so we have enough money."

sentences.zh: 」阿尼便咒之歸。

translations.literal: " Ani at once chanted it back.
translations.idiomatic: " Ani immediately chanted the demon home.

sentences.zh: 數日，貓鬼向素家。

translations.literal: Within several days the cat-demon turned toward Su's household.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the cat-demon was directed at Yang Su's household.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上初從并州還，陀於園中謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向皇后所，使多賜吾物。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Emperor had just returned from Bingzhou, Tuo said to Ani in the garden: "You can make the cat-demon go to the empress's quarters so that she bestows many goods on me."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, soon after the emperor returned from Bingzhou, Tuo told Ani in the garden, "Send the cat-demon to the empress's quarters so she bestows more gifts on me."

sentences.zh: 」阿尼複咒之，遂入宮中。

translations.literal: " Ani again chanted it, and it thereupon entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Ani chanted again, and the demon entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 楊遠乃于門下外省遣阿尼呼貓鬼。

translations.literal: Yang Yuan then, at the outer office of the Gates Department, sent Ani to summon the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuan then had Ani summon the cat-demon at the outer office of the Gates Department.

sentences.zh: 阿尼於是夜中置香粥一盆，以匙扣而呼之曰：「貓女可來，無住宮中。

translations.literal: Ani thereupon at midnight set out a basin of fragrant porridge, knocked it with a spoon, and called: "Cat-girl may come—do not stay in the palace."
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Ani set out a basin of fragrant porridge, tapped it with a spoon, and called, "Cat-girl, come—but do not remain in the palace."

sentences.zh: 」久之，阿尼色正青，若被牽曳者，雲貓鬼已至。

translations.literal: " After a long while Ani's face turned blue-green, as if being dragged, and she said the cat-demon had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: " After a long while Ani's face turned ashen, as if she were being pulled, and she said the cat-demon had arrived.

sentences.zh: 上以其事下公卿，奇章公牛弘曰：「妖由人興，殺其人可以絕矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the matter down to the dukes and ministers; Niuzhang Duke Niu Hong said: "Demons arise through men—kill the man and it can be ended."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the case to the high ministers. Duke Niuzhang Niu Hong said, "Such evil arises through men—execute the man and the matter ends."

sentences.zh: 」上令以犢車載陀夫妻，將賜死於其家。

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered Tuo and his wife loaded on a calf cart and was about to grant death at their home.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered Tuo and his wife placed on a cart and sent home to be executed.

sentences.zh: 陀弟司勳侍中整詣闕求哀，於是免陀死，除名為民，以其妻楊氏為尼。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother, Palace Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel Zheng, went to the gate to beg for mercy; thereupon Tuo's death was remitted, his name was struck off and he was made a commoner, and his wife of the Yang clan was made a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's younger brother Zheng, Palace Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel, pleaded at court for mercy. Tuo's death sentence was remitted; he was stripped of rank and made a commoner, and his wife Lady Yang was forced to become a nun.

sentences.zh: 先是，有人訟其母為人貓鬼所殺者，上以為妖妄，怒而遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, someone had sued that his mother had been killed by another's cat-demon; the Emperor regarded it as demonic falsehood, grew angry, and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man had sued, claiming his mother was killed by another household's cat-demon; the emperor judged it superstitious nonsense, grew angry, and dismissed the case.

sentences.zh: 及此，詔誅被訟行貓鬼家。

translations.literal: At this point an edict ordered the execution of the household sued for practicing the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered the household that had been sued for practicing the cat-demon to be executed.

sentences.zh: 經未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tuo died.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，追念舅氏，聽以禮葬，乃下詔曰：「外氏衰禍，獨孤陀不幸早世，遷卜有期。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, recalling his maternal kin, he permitted burial by ritual and issued an edict saying: "The maternal clan has declined in fortune; Dugu Tuo unhappily died young—the date for moving the tomb is fixed."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, mindful of his mother's kin, he permitted a proper burial and issued an edict: "Our maternal clan has fallen on hard times; Dugu Tuo met an untimely death, and the date for reinterment is now set."

sentences.zh: 言念渭陽之情，追懷傷切，宜加禮命，允備哀榮。

translations.literal: Speaking of the affection at Weiyang, my recollection is deeply wounded; he should receive added ritual honors, fully fitting for mourning glory.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of the bond between uncle and nephew, my grief cuts deep; additional honors are fitting, that mourning may be complete and dignified.

sentences.zh: 可贈正議大夫。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Regular Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously granted the title Regular Counselor.

sentences.zh: 」帝意猶不已，複下詔曰：「舅氏之尊，戚屬斯重，而降年弗永，凋落相繼。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's mind was still not satisfied and he again issued an edict saying: "The honor due maternal uncles, the weight of kin by marriage—yet their allotted years are not long, and one after another they wither and fall."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's grief was not yet spent, and he issued another edict: "Maternal uncles hold a place of honor, and affinal kin weigh heavily in the heart—yet their years are cut short, and one after another they fall away."

sentences.zh: 緬惟先往，宜崇徽秩。

translations.literal: Looking back on those who went before, his noble rank should be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling those who have gone before, his posthumous rank should be elevated.

sentences.zh: 複贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was again posthumously granted Silver-Gleaming Glory Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was again posthumously granted Silver-Gleaming Glory Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 」有二子：延福、延壽。

translations.literal: " He had two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: " He left two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 陀弟整，官至幽州刺史，大業初卒，贈金紫光祿大夫，平鄉侯。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother Zheng reached office as governor of Youzhou; he died at the beginning of Daye and was posthumously granted Gold-Purple Glory Grand Master and made Marquis of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's younger brother Zheng rose to governor of Youzhou; he died early in the Daye era and was posthumously granted Gold-Purple Glory Grand Master and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 蕭巋子琮琮弟瓛

translations.literal: Sons of Xiao Kui: Cong; Cong's younger brother Huan
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Xiao Kui: Xiao Cong; Xiao Cong's Younger Brother Xiao Huan

sentences.zh: 蕭巋，字仁遠，梁昭明太子統之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiao Kui, styled Renyuan, was a grandson of Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui, styled Renyuan, was a grandson of the Liang Crown Prince Zhaoming, Xiao Tong.

sentences.zh: 父詧，初封岳陽王，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: His father Cha was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yueyang and garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao Cha was first enfeoffed Prince of Yueyang and posted to garrison Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，其兄河東王譽與其叔父湘東王繹不協，為繹所害。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, his elder brother Prince of Hedong Yu and his uncle Prince of Xiangdong Yi were at odds, and Yu was killed by Yi.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Kui's elder brother Prince Yu of Hedong fell out with their uncle Prince Xiao Yi of Xiangdong, and Yu was killed by Yi.

sentences.zh: 及繹嗣位，詧稱籓於西魏，乞師請討繹。

translations.literal: When Yi succeeded to the throne, Cha declared himself a vassal to Western Wei, begged troops, and requested to attack Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi took the throne, Cha submitted as a vassal to Western Wei, begged for troops, and asked permission to attack Yi.

sentences.zh: 周太祖以詧為梁主，遣柱國於謹等率騎五萬襲繹，滅之。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou's Grand Ancestor made Cha ruler of Liang and sent Pillar of State Yu Jin and others at the head of fifty thousand horsemen to strike Yi and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Grand Ancestor installed Cha as ruler of Liang and sent Pillar of State Yu Jin with fifty thousand cavalry to strike Yi and destroy him.

sentences.zh: 詧遂都江陵，有荊郡、其西平州延袤三百里之地，稱皇帝于其國，車服節文一同王者。

translations.literal: Cha thereupon moved his capital to Jiangling, holding the Jing commandery and Xiping prefecture to the west—three hundred li in extent—and styled himself emperor in his state; carriage, dress, and ritual regalia were the same as a true king's.
translations.idiomatic: Cha then moved his capital to Jiangling, holding Jing commandery and Xiping prefecture to the west—some three hundred li of territory—and proclaimed himself emperor in his realm, with carriage, dress, and ceremonial regalia matching those of a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 仍置江陵總管，以兵戍之。

translations.literal: A Jiangling area commander was still installed to garrison it with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou still posted an area commander at Jiangling to hold the region with troops.

sentences.zh: 詧薨，巋嗣位，年號天保。

translations.literal: When Cha died, Kui succeeded, with the era name Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha died, Kui succeeded him and took the era name Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 巋俊辯有才學，兼好內典。

translations.literal: Kui was handsome, eloquent, and possessed learning; he also loved Buddhist sutras.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was handsome and eloquent, gifted with learning, and devoted to Buddhist scripture.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊之後，巋來賀，帝享之甚歡。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, Kui came to offer congratulations; the Emperor entertained him with great delight.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, Kui came to offer congratulations; the emperor received him with great delight.

sentences.zh: 親彈琵琶，令巋起舞，巋曰：「陛下親禦五糸玄，臣敢不同百獸！

translations.literal: He personally played the pipa and ordered Kui to dance. Kui said: "Your Majesty personally handles the five-string lute; how dare your servant not join the hundred beasts!"
translations.idiomatic: He played the pipa himself and bade Kui dance. Kui said, "Your Majesty plays the five-string lute himself; how dare I not join the hundred beasts in their dance!"

sentences.zh: 」高祖受禪，恩禮彌厚，遣使賜金五百兩，銀千兩，布帛萬匹，馬五百匹。

translations.literal: " When Gaozu received the abdication, favor and courtesy grew still thicker; he sent envoys bestowing five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silk, and five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, his favor toward Kui grew still deeper; he sent envoys with five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of silk, and five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 巋來朝，上甚敬焉，詔巋位在王公之上。

translations.literal: Kui came to court; the Emperor greatly honored him and decreed that Kui's place should be above kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui came to court, the emperor treated him with exceptional respect and decreed that he should rank above kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 巋被服端麗，進退閒雅，天子矚目，百僚傾慕。

translations.literal: Kui's dress was elegant and refined; his comings and goings were easy and graceful—the Son of Heaven fixed his gaze on him, and the hundred officials looked on with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Kui dressed with elegant refinement and moved with easy grace; the emperor's eyes followed him, and the whole court looked on in admiration.

sentences.zh: 賞賜以億計。

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts ran to the hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and gifts ran into the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 月餘歸籓，帝親餞于滻水之上。

translations.literal: After more than a month he returned to his fief; the Emperor personally saw him off on the banks of the Ba River.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he returned to his domain; the emperor personally saw him off on the banks of the Ba River.

sentences.zh: 後備禮納其女為晉王妃，又欲以其子瑒尚蘭陵公主。

translations.literal: Later, with full ritual, his daughter was taken in as consort to the Prince of Jin; he also wished to marry his son Yang to Princess Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court took his daughter in full ceremony as consort to the Prince of Jin and planned to marry his son Yang to Princess Lanling.

sentences.zh: 由是漸見親待。

translations.literal: From this he gradually came to be treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: From this he gradually won still closer favor.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后言于上曰：「梁主通家，腹心所寄，何勞猜防也。

translations.literal: Empress Xian said to the Emperor: "The Lord of Liang is family by marriage, one in whom you entrust your inmost heart—why trouble yourself with suspicion and guard?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xian told the emperor, "The Lord of Liang is family by marriage, a man you trust with your innermost counsel—why burden yourself with suspicion?"

sentences.zh: 」上然之，於是罷江陵總管，巋專制其國。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved; thereupon the Jiangling area commander was abolished, and Kui held sole authority over his state.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed; the Jiangling area commander was removed, and Kui held sole authority over his realm.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，巋又來朝，賜縑萬匹，珍玩稱是。

translations.literal: After more than a year Kui again came to court and was granted ten thousand bolts of fine silk, with curios and playthings to match.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Kui came to court again and received ten thousand bolts of fine silk and treasures in proportion.

sentences.zh: 及還，上親執手曰：「梁主久滯荊楚，未復舊都，故鄉之念，良軫懷抱。

translations.literal: When he departed, the Emperor personally took his hand and said: "The Lord of Liang has long been detained in Jing-Chu and has not recovered his old capital; thoughts of home truly pierce the heart."
translations.idiomatic: As he departed, the emperor took his hand and said, "You have long been held in Jing-Chu and have not regained your old capital; I know how deeply you long for home."

sentences.zh: 朕當振旅長江，相送旋反耳。

translations.literal: I shall raise an army on the Yangzi and see you safely home again.
translations.idiomatic: I shall march an army to the Yangzi and see you safely restored to your home.

sentences.zh: 」巋拜謝而去。

translations.literal: " Kui bowed in thanks and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Kui bowed in thanks and took his leave.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，寢疾，臨終上表曰：「臣以庸暗，曲荷天慈，寵冠外籓，恩逾連山，爰及子女，尚主婚王。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month he took to his bed with illness and, at life's end, submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant, dim and mediocre, has undeservedly borne Heaven's kindness; favor crowns the outer fiefs, grace surpasses linked mountains—even unto my sons and daughters, marrying them to princesses and princes."
translations.idiomatic: That year in the fifth month he fell ill; on his deathbed he submitted a memorial: "Your servant, unworthy and dull, has yet been showered with Heaven's grace; no vassal prince has known such favor, nor such kindness as yours to my children, given in marriage to imperial princesses and princes."

sentences.zh: 每願躬擐甲胄，身先士卒，掃蕩逋寇，上報明時。

translations.literal: I ever wished to don armor myself, lead the troops from the front, sweep away fleeing bandits, and repay this enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: I had long wished to don armor myself, lead from the front, sweep away the rebels, and repay your enlightened reign.

sentences.zh: 而攝生乖舛，遽罹屙疾，屬纊在辰，顧陰待謝。

translations.literal: Yet nurturing life went awry; suddenly I met with wasting illness—the death-shroud is at hand, and I await dissolution in the shade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my care for life went awry; suddenly wasting illness struck—the death-shroud is near, and I await my end in darkness.

sentences.zh: 長違聖世，感戀嗚咽，遺嗣孤藐，特乞降慈。

translations.literal: Long parted from the sacred age, I sob with yearning love; my orphaned heirs are young and small—I beg especially for lowered mercy.
translations.idiomatic: I must leave your sacred age, and grief chokes my voice; my orphaned heirs are young and helpless—I beg your mercy upon them.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖躬與山嶽同固，皇基等天日俱永，臣雖九泉，實無遣恨。

translations.literal: I bow and wish that Your Sacred Person may be firm as mountains and hills, and the imperial foundation as enduring as Heaven and sun together; though your servant reaches the nine springs, truly there is no lingering regret.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty's person may stand firm as the mountains, and the imperial foundation endure as Heaven and sun; though I go to the grave, I shall have no regret.

sentences.zh: 」並獻所服金裝劍，上覽而嗟悼焉。

translations.literal: " He also presented the gold-mounted sword he had worn; when the Emperor read it he sighed in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: " He also presented the gold-mounted sword he had worn. The emperor read the memorial and mourned deeply.

sentences.zh: 巋在位二十三年，年四十四薨，梁之臣子諡曰孝明皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: Kui reigned twenty-three years and died at age forty-four; Liang's ministers and subjects gave him the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoming, with temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Kui had reigned twenty-three years and died at forty-four; Liang's ministers gave him the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoming, with temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 子琮嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiao Cong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 巋著《孝經》、《周易義記》及《大小乘幽微》十四卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Kui authored "Classic of Filial Piety," "Record of the Meanings of the Book of Changes," and "Subtleties of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles" in fourteen scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Kui wrote the Classic of Filial Piety, Record of the Meanings of the Book of Changes, and Subtleties of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles in fourteen scrolls, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 琮字溫文，性寬仁，有大度，倜儻不羈，博學有文義。

translations.literal: Cong, styled Wenwen, was by nature generous and humane, possessed great breadth, was free-spirited and unrestrained, and was broadly learned with literary understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cong, styled Wenwen, was generous and humane by nature, magnanimous, free-spirited and unrestrained, broadly learned, and skilled in letters.

sentences.zh: 兼善弓馬，遣人伏地著帖，琮馳馬射之，十發十中，持帖者亦不懼。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in bow and horse; he had a man lie prone holding a target-placard, Cong galloped and shot at it—ten shots, ten hits—and the man holding the placard was not afraid.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled with bow and horse. He would have a man lie prone holding a target, then gallop and shoot—ten shots, ten hits—while the man holding the target never flinched.

sentences.zh: 初封東陽王，尋立為梁太子。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang and soon after established as Liang crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed Prince of Dongyang and soon named crown prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，上賜璽書曰：「負荷堂構，其事甚重，雖窮憂勞，常須自力。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, the Emperor bestowed an imperial letter saying: "Bearing the burden of the ancestral hall is a weighty matter; though exhausted with cares and toil, you must constantly rely on your own strength."
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded, the emperor sent an imperial letter: "To bear the burden of the ancestral temple is a grave matter; though care and toil wear you down, you must ever rely on your own strength."

sentences.zh: 輯諧內外，親任才良，聿遵世業，是所望也。

translations.literal: Harmonize within and without, personally employ the talented and good, and duly follow the work of generations—this is what is hoped.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonize within and without, personally entrust the talented, and duly uphold your forebears' work—this is what I expect of you.

sentences.zh: 彼之疆守，咫尺陳人，水潦之時，特宜警備。

translations.literal: Their border garrisons are a foot's distance from Chen men; in times of flood it is especially fitting to stay alert and prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Your border lies a stone's throw from Chen; in flood season you must be especially vigilant.

sentences.zh: 陳氏比日雖複朝聘相尋，疆埸之間猶未清肅，唯當恃我必不可幹，勿得輕人而不設備。

translations.literal: Though the Chen clan of late has again sent envoys in succession, between the border marches things are still not clear and settled; you should rely only on me as one who cannot be meddled with—do not slight others and fail to set defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chen has lately resumed embassies, the frontier is not yet secure. Trust that no one may challenge me—but do not therefore slight your neighbor or neglect your defenses.

sentences.zh: 朕與梁國，積世相知，重以親姻，情義彌厚。

translations.literal: I and the state of Liang have known each other through accumulated generations; redoubled by marriage kin, affection and righteousness grow ever thicker.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and I have known each other across generations; bound now by marriage, our affection runs still deeper.

sentences.zh: 江陵之地，朝寄非輕，為國為民，深宜抑割，恆加饘粥，以禮自存。

translations.literal: The land of Jiangling is no light charge from the court; for state and for people you should deeply restrain yourself, constantly take thin gruel, and preserve yourself by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling is no light charge from the court; for your state and your people you must restrain yourself deeply, live frugally on plain gruel, and keep yourself by ritual discipline.

sentences.zh: 」又賜梁之大臣璽書，誠勉之。

translations.literal: " He also bestowed imperial letters on Liang's great ministers, sincerely exhorting them.
translations.idiomatic: " He also sent imperial letters to Liang's senior ministers, earnestly exhorting them.

sentences.zh: 時琮年號廣運，有識者曰：「運之為字，軍走也，吾君將奔走乎？

translations.literal: At that time Cong's era name was Guangyun; men of insight said: "As for the character yun, within it are jun and zou—'army' and 'walk'—will our lord take to flight?"
translations.idiomatic: Cong's era name was Guangyun; men of insight said, "The character yun contains jun and zou—'army' and 'walk'—will our lord be put to flight?"

sentences.zh: 」其年，琮遣大將軍戚昕以舟師襲陳公安，不克而還。

translations.literal: " That year Cong sent Grand General Qi Xin with a river force to strike Chen's An'gong but did not overcome him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " That year Cong sent Grand General Qi Xin with a fleet against Chen's An'gong but failed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 征琮叔父岑入朝，拜為大將軍，封懷義公，因留不遣。

translations.literal: He summoned Cong's uncle Cen to court, appointed him Grand General, enfeoffed him as Duke of Huaiyi, and detained him without sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned Cong's uncle Cen to court, appointed him Grand General, enfeoffed him Duke of Huaiyi, and kept him there.

sentences.zh: 複置江陵總管以監之。

translations.literal: The Jiangling area commander was again installed to oversee him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangling area commander was reinstated to keep watch over him.

sentences.zh: 琮所署大將軍許世武密以城召陳將宜黃侯陳紀，謀泄，琮誅之。

translations.literal: Grand General Xu Shiwu, whom Cong had appointed, secretly used the city to summon Chen's general Marquis of Yihuang Chen Ji; the plot leaked and Cong executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Xu Shiwu, whom Cong had appointed, secretly offered the city to Chen's Marquis of Yihuang, Chen Ji; when the plot was exposed, Cong had him executed.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，上征琮入朝，率其臣下二百余人朝于京師，江陵父老莫不隕涕相謂曰：「吾君其不反矣！

translations.literal: Two years later the Emperor summoned Cong to court; he led more than two hundred of his ministers and subordinates to attend at the capital. The elders of Jiangling all shed tears and said to one another: "Our lord surely will not return!"
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor summoned Cong to court; he led more than two hundred ministers and officials to the capital. The elders of Jiangling wept and said to one another, "Our lord will never come back!"

sentences.zh: 」上以琮來朝，遣武鄉公崔弘度將兵戍之。

translations.literal: " Because Cong had come to court, he sent Duke of Wuxiang Cui Hongdu to lead troops to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: " Because Cong had come to court, the emperor sent Duke of Wuxiang Cui Hongdu with troops to garrison Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 軍至鄀州，琮叔父岩及弟瓛等懼弘度掩襲之，遂引陳人至城下，虜居民而叛，於是廢梁國。

translations.literal: When the army reached Ruozhou, Cong's uncle Yan and younger brother Huan and others feared Hongdu would launch a surprise attack; they thereupon brought Chen men to the foot of the wall, seized the inhabitants, and rebelled—whereupon the state of Liang was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Ruozhou, Cong's uncle Yan and his younger brother Huan, fearing a surprise attack by Hongdu, brought Chen troops to the walls, seized the populace, and rebelled; Liang was abolished.

sentences.zh: 上遣左僕射高熲安集之，曲赦江陵死罪，給民複十年。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to pacify and gather them; he specially pardoned capital crimes in Jiangling and granted the people tax relief for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to pacify the region, specially pardoned capital offenses in Jiangling, and granted the people ten years' tax relief.

sentences.zh: 梁二主各給守墓十戶。

translations.literal: To each of the two Liang lords ten households were given to tend their tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the two Liang rulers was granted ten households to tend their tombs.

sentences.zh: 拜琮為柱國，賜爵莒國公。

translations.literal: Cong was appointed Pillar of State and granted the title Duke of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was appointed Pillar of State and enfeoffed Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，以皇后之故，甚見親重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, because of the empress he was greatly favored and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, Cong was greatly favored because of the empress.

sentences.zh: 拜內史令，改封梁公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and re-enfeoffed Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 琮之宗族，緦麻以上，並隨才擢用，於是諸蕭昆弟布列朝廷。

translations.literal: Cong's clansmen, from those in the lowest mourning grade upward, were all promoted according to talent; thus the various Xiao brothers were spread through the court.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's kinsmen, even those in the lowest degree of mourning relationship, were promoted according to ability, and Xiao clansmen filled the court.

sentences.zh: 琮性淡雅，不以職務自嬰，退朝縱酒而已。

translations.literal: Cong was by nature refined and detached; he did not burden himself with official duties—after court he merely indulged in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was refined and detached by nature; he did not burden himself with office and, after court, merely drank his fill.

sentences.zh: 內史令楊約與琮同列，帝令約宣旨誡勵，約複以私情喻之。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Yang Yue held the same rank as Cong; the Emperor ordered Yue to proclaim the edict admonishing and encouraging him, and Yue again used private feeling to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Director Yang Yue held the same rank as Cong; the emperor ordered Yue to convey an admonition, and Yue spoke to him as a friend.

sentences.zh: 琮答曰：「琮若複事事，則何異於公哉！

translations.literal: Cong replied: "If Cong again attended to every matter, how would that differ from you, sir!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong replied, "If I attended to every matter, how would I differ from you?"

sentences.zh: 」約笑而退。

translations.literal: " Yue laughed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue laughed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 約兄素，時為尚書令，見琮嫁從父妹于鉗耳氏，因謂琮曰：「公，帝王之族，望高戚美，何乃適妹鉗耳氏乎？

translations.literal: Yue's elder brother Su was then Director of the Department of State Affairs; seeing Cong marry a younger cousin of his father's generation to the Qian'er clan, he therefore said to Cong: "Sir, you are of an imperial house—your standing is high and your affinal kin splendid—why marry your sister to the Qian'er clan?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue's elder brother Yang Su was then Director of the Department of State Affairs. Seeing Cong marry a paternal cousin to the Qian'er clan, he said, "You are of an imperial house, of high standing and splendid connections—why give your cousin to the Qian'er clan?"

sentences.zh: 」琮曰：「前已嫁妹于侯莫陳氏，此複何疑！

translations.literal: " Cong said: "Earlier I already married a sister to the Houmobochen clan—what doubt is there about this!"
translations.idiomatic: " Cong said, "I already married one sister to the Houmobochen clan—what is there to question now?"

sentences.zh: 」素曰：「鉗耳，羌也，侯莫陳，虜也，何得相比！

translations.literal: " Su said: "Qian'er are Qiang; Houmobochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"
translations.idiomatic: " Su said, "The Qian'er are Qiang; the Houmobochen are barbarians—how can you compare them!"

sentences.zh: 」素意以虜優羌劣。

translations.literal: " Su's meaning was that barbarians were superior and Qiang inferior.
translations.idiomatic: " Su meant that barbarians ranked above Qiang.

sentences.zh: 琮曰：「以羌異虜，未之前聞。

translations.literal: Cong said: "That Qiang differ from barbarians—I have never heard it before."
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, "That Qiang differ from barbarians—I have never heard such a thing."

sentences.zh: 」素慚而止。

translations.literal: " Su, ashamed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Su, ashamed, said no more.

sentences.zh: 琮雖羈旅，見北間豪貴，無所降下。

translations.literal: Though Cong was a detained guest, when he met the great and noble of the north he showed no deference.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cong lived as a captive guest in the north, he showed no deference before its great families.

sentences.zh: 嘗與賀若弼深相友善，弼既被誅，複有童謠曰：「蕭蕭亦複起。

translations.literal: He had once been deeply friendly with He Ruo Bi; after Bi was executed, there was again a children's song saying: "Xiao, Xiao will rise again."
translations.idiomatic: He had once been close friends with He Ruo Bi; after Bi was executed, a children's rhyme ran, "The Xiao, the Xiao will rise again."

sentences.zh: 」帝由是忌之，遂廢於家，未幾而卒。

translations.literal: " The Emperor from this grew jealous of him, had him removed to his home, and before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grew suspicious of him, had him confined at home, and before long he died.

sentences.zh: 贈左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Glory Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Left Glory Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 子鉉，襄城通守。

translations.literal: His son Xian was Defender-in-Chief of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian served as Defender-in-Chief of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 複以琮弟子钜為梁公。

translations.literal: Cong's younger brother's son Ju was again made Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's nephew Ju was again enfeoffed Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 钜小名藏，煬帝甚昵之，以為千牛，與宇文皛出入宮掖，伺察內外。

translations.literal: Ju, whose childhood name was Cang, was greatly favored by Emperor Yang; he was made a Thousand-Ox Guard and, with Yuwen Hao, went in and out of the palace women's quarters, spying on affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Ju, childhood name Cang, was greatly favored by Emperor Yang, appointed to the Thousand-Ox Guard, and with Yuwen Hao moved freely through the inner palace, watching affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 帝每有遊宴，钜未嘗不從焉，遂于宮中多行淫穢。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor had outings and banquets, Ju never failed to follow; he thereupon committed many lewd and filthy acts within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor held outings or banquets, Ju was always in attendance, and he committed many lewd acts within the palace.

sentences.zh: 江都之變，為宇文化及所殺。

translations.literal: At the Jiangdu upheaval he was killed by Yuwen Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiangdu upheaval he was killed by Yuwen Huaji.

sentences.zh: 瓛字欽文，少聰敏，解屬文。

translations.literal: Huan, styled Qinwen, was in youth clever and keen and skilled in composing literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Huan, styled Qinwen, was clever as a youth and skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 在梁為荊州刺史，頗有能名。

translations.literal: In Liang he was governor of Jingzhou and had a considerable reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as governor of Jingzhou and won a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 崔弘度以兵至若阝州，瓛懼，與其叔父岩奔于陳。

translations.literal: When Cui Hongdu came with troops to Ruozhou, Huan was afraid; with his uncle Yan he fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hongdu advanced on Ruozhou with troops, Huan, in fear, fled to Chen with his uncle Yan.

sentences.zh: 陳主以為侍中、安東將軍、吳州刺史，甚得物情，三吳父老皆曰：「瓛吾君子也。

translations.literal: The Chen sovereign made him Palace Attendant, Pacifying-East General, and governor of Wuzhou; he greatly won popular sentiment, and the elders of the Three Wu all said: "Huan is our gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor appointed him Palace Attendant, Pacifying-East General, and governor of Wuzhou; he won great popular affection, and the elders of the Three Wu said, "Huan is our true gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」及陳亡，吳人推瓛為主。

translations.literal: " When Chen perished, the people of Wu pushed Huan as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: " When Chen fell, the people of Wu rallied to Huan as their leader.

sentences.zh: 吳人見梁武、簡文及詧、巋等兄弟並第三而踐尊位，瓛自以巋之第三子也，深自矜負。

translations.literal: The people of Wu saw that Liang's Emperor Wu, Emperor Jianwen, and the brothers Cha, Kui, and others had all been third sons when they ascended the honored position; Huan took himself to be Kui's third son and deeply prided himself on it.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu noted that Emperor Wu of Liang, Emperor Jianwen, and the brothers Cha and Kui had all been third sons when they took the throne; Huan, as Kui's third son, took great pride in the omen.

sentences.zh: 有謝異者，頗知廢興，梁、陳之際，言無不驗，江南人甚敬信之。

translations.literal: There was one Xie Yi who was well versed in rise and fall; in the interval between Liang and Chen, his words never failed to come true, and the people of Jiangnan greatly revered and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Xie Yi who could read the rise and fall of dynasties; in the transition from Liang to Chen, his words never failed, and the people of Jiangnan revered him.

sentences.zh: 及陳主被擒，異奔於瓛，由是益為眾所歸。

translations.literal: When the Chen sovereign was captured, Yi fled to Huan; from this he was still more followed by the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen emperor was captured, Yi fled to Huan, and the people rallied to Huan still more.

sentences.zh: 褒國公宇文述以兵討之，瓛遣王哀守吳州，自將拒述。

translations.literal: Duke of Baiguo Yuwen Shu came with troops to attack him; Huan sent Wang Ai to hold Wuzhou and personally led the army to resist Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Baiguo Yuwen Shu marched against him; Huan sent Wang Ai to hold Wuzhou and led the army himself to resist Shu.

sentences.zh: 述遣兵別道襲吳州，哀懼，衣道士服，棄城而遁。

translations.literal: Shu sent troops by a separate route to strike Wuzhou; Ai was afraid, put on Taoist robes, abandoned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shu sent a detachment by another route against Wuzhou; Ai, in fear, donned Taoist robes, abandoned the city, and fled.

sentences.zh: 瓛眾聞之，悉無鬥志，與述一戰而敗。

translations.literal: When Huan's host heard this, all lost fighting spirit; after one battle with Shu they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's army, hearing this, lost all will to fight; one battle with Shu and they were broken.

sentences.zh: 瓛將左右數人逃於太湖，匿於民家，為人所執，送於述所，斬之長安，時年二十一。

translations.literal: Huan led a few men of his entourage in flight to Lake Tai, hid in a commoner's house, was seized by someone, sent to Shu's place, and executed at Chang'an—he was then twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Huan fled to Lake Tai with a few followers, hid in a commoner's house, was seized and sent to Shu, and was executed at Chang'an at the age of twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 弟璟，為朝請大夫、尚衣奉禦。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jing was Court Consultant and Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jing served as Court Consultant and Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 瑒，曆衛尉卿、秘書監、陶丘侯。

translations.literal: Yang successively held the posts of Commandant of the Guards, Director of the Palace Library, and was Marquis of Taoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang served successively as Commandant of the Guards and Director of the Palace Library and was enfeoffed Marquis of Taoqiu.

sentences.zh: 瑀，曆內史侍郎、河池太守。

translations.literal: Yu successively held Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and was governor of Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu served successively as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and governor of Hechi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：三五哲王，防深慮遠，舅甥之國，罕執鈞衡，母后之家，無聞傾敗。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The sage kings of the Three Five eras guarded deeply and thought far ahead; states of uncle and nephew seldom held the balance of power; the families of empresses dowager were unheard of in ruinous collapse.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The sage kings of antiquity looked far ahead and guarded against danger; states ruled by uncle and nephew seldom held real power, and empresses' kin were rarely heard of in ruinous collapse.

sentences.zh: 爰及漢、晉，顛覆繼軌，皆由乎進不以禮，故其斃亦速。

translations.literal: Down to Han and Jin, overthrow followed in succession—all because advancement was not by ritual, and therefore their destruction was also swift.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Han and Jin, ruin followed ruin in turn, all because advancement came without proper restraint—and so their fall came quickly as well.

sentences.zh: 若使獨孤權侔呂、霍，必敗于仁壽之前，蕭氏勢均梁、竇，豈全于大業之後！

translations.literal: Had the Dugu clan's power matched that of Lü and Huo, they would surely have been ruined before Renshou; had the Xiao clan's strength equaled that of Liang and Dou, how could they have been preserved after Daye!
translations.idiomatic: Had the Dugu kin wielded power like the Lü and Huo clans, they would surely have fallen before the Renshou era; had the Xiao kin matched the might of the Liang and Dou houses, how could they have survived into Daye!

sentences.zh: 今或不隕舊基，或更隆先構，豈非處之以道，不預權寵之所致乎！

translations.literal: That some today did not fall from their former foundations, or even raised their ancestors' structures higher—is this not the result of treating them by the Way and not letting them share in power and favor!
translations.idiomatic: That some today did not lose their ancestral standing, or even surpassed their forebears' estate—is this not precisely because the Sui treated them with proper restraint and kept them from court power and favor!
